entries.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting | How to Create 3D Gaussian Splatting From Drone Video Beginner Guide
entries.summary: Capture one DJI drone video with GPS video subtitles, locked white balance, 4K/30fps normal color, ISO 100 and ~1/60 shutter, orbit the subject, then process into a Gaussian splat with Mip-Map.

skills.name: dji-video-capture-for-gaussian-splat
skills.goal: Record a geo-referenced drone video for splatting.
steps: Power on DJI drone and climb to subject height.
Switch to video mode; enable Video Subtitles (GPS per frame).
Set WB to Auto then lock it; set 4K 30fps Normal color.
Set ISO 100 and shutter ~1/60 (or lighting-appropriate).
Fly a smooth multi-angle orbit with overlap; land and copy the video.

skills.name: process-drone-video-to-gaussian-splat-mipmap
skills.goal: Build a splat from that video in Mip-Map.
steps: Import the video into Mip-Map.
Extract frames using subtitle GPS when present.
Run Gaussian splat reconstruction.
Inspect and export the 3D splat.

entries.title: How to Do Drone Gaussian Splatting: Beginner Tutorial (Splatware)

skills.name: drone-hyperlapse-multi-angle-capture
skills.goal: Capture overlapping views with DJI hyperlapse.
steps: Plan multi-angle coverage of every facade (photogrammetry-style).
Use DJI built-in hyperlapse modes.
Fly slowly; avoid blur; export media.

skills.name: upload-capture-to-free-splatware
skills.goal: Process capture in free Splatware.
steps: Open free Splatware web app.
Upload hyperlapse/video.
Run processing; review and download the splat.

entries.title: Drone Video to 3D Gaussian Splat in the Browser Tutorial

entries.title: EDIT PHOTOS Like a Pro // Complete LIGHTROOM Tutorial
entries.summary: Start-to-finish Lightroom workflow: choose a strong Library image, note light and composition, then Develop with an efficient ordered edit and export.

skills.name: lightroom-select-and-develop-photo
skills.goal: Edit one photo end-to-end in Lightroom.
steps: In Library, pick a strong base photo.
Open Develop on the unedited version.
Set global exposure, contrast, and white balance for the light.
Add local adjustments to separate subject from background.
Refine color/crop; export final file.

entries.title: Python Tutorial: Pathlib - The Modern Way to Handle File Paths

skills.name: python-pathlib-basic-file-workflow
skills.goal: Common file tasks with pathlib.
steps: from pathlib import Path
Build paths with Path.cwd()/Path.home() and the / operator.
Use exists(), mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True).
read_text/write_text; iterdir/glob for listing.
Prefer Path objects over string concatenation.

entries.title: Distill transcript (library pipeline skill)
entries.summary: Reusable skill: take a raw YouTube-provided transcript file, strip filler and sponsorship, keep only actionable steps and key facts needed to reproduce the how-to.

skills.name: distill-transcript
skills.goal: Turn raw caption text into actionable procedure lines.
steps: Read the raw transcript file for one video (YouTube-provided captions only).
Remove filler: um/uh, greetings, sponsorship, subscribe CTAs, pure hype.
Keep sentences that state settings, clicks, tool names, order of operations, constraints (file size, ISO, fps, etc.).
Deduplicate near-repeat lines; order chronologically when the transcript order is clear.
Write distilled.json and distilled.md under distilled/<video_id>/ (until user confirms final summary location).
From the distilled lines, emit or refresh executable skill steps under skills/<name>.md and merge into LIBRARY.json.

entries.title: ABSOLUTE Beginner Basics.. Blender For Noobs 2025
entries.summary: Viewport nav, Object/Edit mode, G/S/R/E, loop cut, bevel, then a low-poly pine from primitives.

skills.name: blender-viewport-navigation-mmb
skills.goal: Orbit, pan, zoom, and snap orthographic views in Blender's 3D viewport.
steps: Scroll the middle mouse wheel to zoom in and out.
Click and drag the middle mouse button to orbit around the object.
Hold Shift and middle-mouse-drag to pan the scene.
If you have a numpad: 1 front orthographic, 3 right, 7 top, 9 bottom.
Without a numpad: hold Alt, middle-mouse-drag toward the desired axis to snap orthographic views.

skills.name: blender-edit-mode-transform-extrude-loopcut-bevel
skills.goal: Switch Object/Edit mode and use core mesh edit hotkeys (G/S/R/E, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+B).
steps: Select the mesh; use Object mode for whole-object transforms (G grab/move).
Enter Edit mode (Tab) to edit vertices, edges, or faces; switch selection modes for verts/edges/faces.
Press A to select all; S to scale selection; R to rotate (optionally R then Y/X/Z to axis-lock).
Select a face and press E to extrude; axis-lock with E then Z (or X/Y) when needed.
Press Ctrl+R for a loop cut; scroll wheel for multiple cuts; click to confirm.
Alt-select an edge loop; Ctrl+B to bevel; scroll wheel to add bevel segments.
Optional: right-click Shade Smooth / Auto Smooth for softer shading without micro-bevels.

skills.name: blender-lowpoly-pine-tree-from-primitives
skills.goal: Build a simple low-poly pine tree using cylinder and circle meshes with extrude/scale/duplicate.
steps: Delete unneeded default mesh if present.
Shift+A → Mesh → Cylinder; in Add Cylinder adjust vertices down (e.g. 8) for low poly.
Tab Edit mode; scale trunk; select top face, move up, S scale for trunk taper; optional Shade Smooth Auto Smooth.
Shift+A → Mesh → Circle (e.g. 12 sides).
Edit mode, edge select; E then Z to extrude on Z; S scale; Ctrl+R loop cuts and scale for foliage layers.
L select linked pieces as needed; Shift+D duplicate foliage layers; R/S (and R then Z) to vary layers.
Stack scaled/rotated circle extrusions above the trunk for a pine silhouette.

entries.title: Watch This Before you Get Started with Blender (7 Tips)
entries.summary: Learning map, simplify UI to Layout, three-button mouse nav, shortcuts, geometry practice, add meshes.

skills.name: blender-beginner-setup-nav-and-geometry-practice
skills.goal: Start Blender the right way: Layout workspace focus, three-button mouse nav, G/S/R, Edit mode verts/edges/faces, then freeform practice.
steps: Write a short learning map: end goal plus key concepts/procedures to learn (skip unrelated tutorials).
Open Blender; select Layout workspace; mentally ignore top menus, Outliner, Properties, Timeline—focus on 3D Viewport and default cube.
Use a three-button mouse: scroll zoom; MMB drag orbit; Shift+MMB pan. Practice small incremental orbits from screen center.
Object mode: G grab/move, S scale, R rotate the cube; click to confirm.
Tab into Edit mode. Selection modes: 1 vertex, 2 edge, 3 face. G/R/S components; Shift-click or box-select (wireframe for through-select).
Tab to Object mode; Shift+A → Mesh to add primitives at the 3D cursor; G to place; edit in Edit mode.
Delete extras in Object mode with Shift+X, Enter. Build rough recognizable shapes without tutorials to cement fundamentals.

entries.title: Blender Tutorial – How to Use AI to Create 3D Models (ChatGPT and Blender)
entries.summary: Generate Blender Python via ChatGPT, run in Scripting workspace, iterate on errors.

skills.name: blender-chatgpt-python-script-gold-ball
skills.goal: Use ChatGPT to generate a Blender Python script, paste it in the Scripting workspace, and run it to create a material-previewable object.
steps: Install/launch Blender from blender.org; dismiss splash.
Open chat.openai.com; prompt e.g. write a Blender script that creates a gold ball (include the word script).
Copy the code block from ChatGPT.
In Blender, select default cube, press X and confirm delete for a blank start.
Open Scripting workspace tab → New → paste (Ctrl/Cmd+V).
Click Run; switch back to Layout; enable Material Preview shading to see material color.
If the script errors, copy the error into ChatGPT and retry with the fixed script.

entries.title: Learning BLENDER as a GAME DEV
entries.summary: Advice: low-poly focus, early engine export, structured practice (thin on UI steps).

skills.name: blender-gamedev-learning-path-advice
skills.goal: Follow a game-dev-oriented Blender learning order: basics → low-poly assets → early engine export → optional sculpt/bake.
steps: Optionally do a short beginner control/UI tutorial (donut parts early only if used).
Prioritize low-poly game-asset fundamentals where polygon count matters over dense non-game scenes.
Export a simple mesh to your game engine as early as possible; fix export issues before detailing.
Practice easy low-poly models on your own; then study rigging; later sculpting and baking high-to-low when needed.
Finish a small personal/game-jam asset project end-to-end for retention.

entries.title: How to 3D Model Using Blender - Easy Beginner Guide + Tips and Tricks
entries.summary: Millimeter scene setup and Boolean-cut bracket with cylinder hole cutters.

skills.name: blender-metric-mm-setup-for-3d-print
skills.goal: Configure Blender scene units and grid to millimeters for dimension-accurate hard-surface / 3D-print modeling.
steps: Open Scene Properties; set Unit System to Metric.
Set Unit Scale to 0.001 and Length to Millimeters.
Open Viewport Overlays; set grid Scale to 0.001 so the grid matches mm.
Select object; press N for Sidebar; confirm Location/Rotation/Scale/Dimensions read in mm.
Reset object location to 0,0,0 if recentering at origin.

skills.name: blender-boolean-bracket-with-cylinder-holes
skills.goal: Model a simple mm bracket plate and cut bolt holes with cylinder Boolean Difference.
steps: Optional: delete Camera and Light (right-click Delete) to declutter.
Set cube dimensions for the plate (e.g. 100 mm wide, 12 deep, 3 thick); rename to bracket.
Add → Mesh → Cylinder; before confirming, open Add Cylinder panel and raise Vertices (e.g. 256).
Size cutter diameter with clearance (e.g. 5.6 mm) and height taller than plate (e.g. 10 mm); rename hole cutter.
Duplicate cutters, position along plate (set Location numerically); Shift-select cutters → Join into one cutter object.
Select bracket → Modifiers → Add Boolean → Object = hole cutter, Operation Difference → Apply.
Delete cutter object(s); verify holes. Tab Edit mode; Face select; E extrude an edge/face to form an L-bracket flange as needed.
Optional: enable MeasureIt add-on (Edit→Preferences→Add-ons) to measure hole diameters in mm.

entries.title: The World's Easiest Blender Tutorial for Beginners
entries.summary: Easy car blockout with loop cut, extrude, inset, apply transforms, cylinder wheels.

skills.name: blender-easy-car-box-model-core-tools
skills.goal: Block out a simple car using scale-axis locks, loop cut, extrude, inset, apply transforms, and duplicated wheels.
steps: Select cube; S then Y stretch length; S then Z flatten height to a car-body proportion.
Tab Edit mode; A select all; Ctrl+R loop cut (scroll for 2 cuts); place cuts; wireframe view to move side verts for body shape.
Face select roof region; E extrude upward; pull windshield verts back on Y for rake.
Object mode Ctrl+A Apply All Transforms; Edit mode again; select window faces; I inset then E extrude inward for glass recesses.
Object mode; Shift+A Mesh → Cylinder for a tire; S and S+Z to tire proportions; Edit mode I/E for hub detail.
Front orthographic view; R rotate tire with Ctrl for snapped angle; rename objects; duplicate wheels to four corners.

entries.title: Blender Low Poly Character Modeling Tutorial - Part 1
entries.summary: Eevee + Standard color management, incremental saves, reference images, Rigify metarig scale.

skills.name: blender-lowpoly-character-scene-prep
skills.goal: Prepare a Blender 4+ scene for stylized low-poly character work: Eevee, Standard view transform, incremental saves, image references, Rigify metarig scale.
steps: Render Properties: Engine Eevee; ensure Ambient Occlusion, Bloom, Screen Space Reflections, Motion Blur off.
Color Management → View Transform → Standard.
Delete default cube if desired; File → Save As into a project folder; use Ctrl+S often and Ctrl+Alt+S for incremental saves.
Shift+A → Image → Reference; import front and side images.
Edit → Preferences → Add-ons → enable Rigify; Shift+A → Armature → Human Meta-Rig for human scale.
Select both references; front ortho view; Alt+G/Alt+S/Alt+R reset as needed; R then X 90 to stand images up.
G/S and axis locks (G+Z, G+Y, R+Z 90) to align feet to ground and match metarig height; set reference Opacity ~0.5.

entries.title: Blender Tutorial for Beginners
entries.summary: Install/prefs, model cookie+chips+tray, materials, area light, camera lock, render.

skills.name: blender-install-preferences-and-viewport-basics
skills.goal: Install Blender, set useful preferences, and learn viewport nav plus G/R/S and Object/Edit mode.
steps: Download Blender from blender.org and install for your OS; open and click outside splash to dismiss.
Edit → Preferences → Interface: adjust Resolution Scale if UI is tiny/huge.
Preferences → System: enable CUDA/GPU Cycles device if available; raise Undo Steps (e.g. 100); Save Preferences.
Viewport: MMB orbit, Shift+MMB pan, scroll zoom; optional gizmo orbit/zoom/pan; numpad/gizmo axis views.
Learn Move/Rotate/Scale tools and hotkeys G, R, S; axis-constrain with X/Y/Z; Tab for Edit mode.

skills.name: blender-chocolate-chip-cookie-model-and-render
skills.goal: Model a cookie with chips on a tray, assign materials, light with an Area light, frame camera, and render.
steps: Object mode: add Cylinder as cookie base (Shift while drawing for 1:1 circle); scale Z flatter; right-click Shade Smooth; rename to cookie.
Shift+A → Mesh → UV Sphere for a chip; S scale; G then Z place into cookie; Shade Smooth; Shift+D duplicate many chips.
Add thin Cube tray (Shift for square); Tab Edit mode; face select top; I inset; Extrude region downward for tray lip; Tab Object mode; position under cookie.
Select cookie → Material Properties → New → set Base Color (eyedropper optional); switch Viewport to Material Preview.
Select one chip → set dark Base Color; Shift-select all chips ending on the colored one; Ctrl+L → Link Materials.
Material on tray (e.g. blue). Delete default light; Shift+A → Light → Area; raise Power (~800–850), lower temperature (~4000K); move/rotate to light cookie.
Numpad 0 camera view; N → View → Lock Camera to View; compose shot; uncheck Lock Camera to View.
Render Properties: choose Eevee or Cycles (GPU if available); Render → Render Image (F12); Image → Save As.

entries.title: Blender Beginner Tutorial - Part 1
entries.summary: Resolution scale, Move/Rotate/Scale tools, viewport navigation foundations.

skills.name: blender-beginner-three-tools-and-viewport-nav
skills.goal: Learn Move/Rotate/Scale tools and MMB viewport navigation (with trackpad alternatives) as absolute beginner foundations.
steps: Edit → Preferences → set Resolution Scale (e.g. 1.25) so UI is readable.
Activate Move tool; drag RGB handles to move the cube.
Activate Rotate tool; drag handles to rotate.
Activate Scale tool; drag the white uniform handle to scale on all axes.
Navigate: MMB orbit, Shift+MMB pan, scroll zoom (use Emulate 3 Button Mouse / trackpad alternatives if needed).

entries.title: Getting started - Blender for complete beginners
entries.summary: Add/delete meshes, focus selection, F3 search, save .blend, camera view.

skills.name: blender-complete-beginner-add-delete-focus
skills.goal: After basic navigation, delete/add mesh objects, focus selection, use F3 search, and save the .blend.
steps: Dismiss splash; practice orbit/pan/zoom; use View Selected (numpad period) if lost.
Learn F3 operator search (context-sensitive to Object mode vs elsewhere).
File → Save As to create your .blend early.
Select default cube; X → Delete (Enter) to remove it.
Shift+A → Mesh → add primitives (cube, monkey, etc.); practice add/delete.
Numpad 0 (or camera icon) to preview camera framing used for renders.

entries.title: Beginner Blender Tutorial (2026)
entries.summary: Donut-series foundations: nav, add mesh, shade smooth; mug with Solidify/Subsurf/loop cuts.

skills.name: blender-donut-tutorial-nav-add-shade-smooth
skills.goal: Start the Blender Guru beginner path: install/open Blender, navigate, delete cube, add torus/cylinder, shade smooth, learn G/R/S.
steps: Download Blender 5.x (or current) from blender.org; install or use portable zip; open and click off splash.
Orbit MMB-drag; Shift+MMB pan; scroll zoom; use axis gizmo clicks if upside-down.
Optional: Preferences → Interface Resolution Scale for readable UI; Input Emulate 3 Button Mouse if no MMB.
Delete default cube (X → Delete).
Shift+A → Mesh add (torus for donut path / cylinder for mug path); adjust Add last-operation settings before clicking away.
Right-click object → Shade Smooth when appropriate.
Practice G/R/S; Tab Edit mode to edit geometry; return to Object mode to select other objects.

skills.name: blender-mug-solidify-subsurf-loopcut
skills.goal: Block a coffee mug from a cylinder using Edit mode, Solidify, Subdivision Surface, and Ctrl+R loop cuts (from Blender Guru beginner series).
steps: Add/position cylinder as mug; Tab Edit mode; shape walls (scale loops) toward a mug silhouette.
Add Solidify modifier for wall thickness; adjust thickness non-destructively.
Add Subdivision Surface; raise Viewport levels carefully; note how unchecked edges become overly round.
Ctrl+R add loop cuts near rim/base to hold shape under Subsurf; slide and confirm.
Use reference image (Add Image Reference); clear bad rotation, set 90° with Ctrl-snap; scale to match mug.
Before handle extrudes: Apply Solidify so inner/outer walls are real mesh; then extrude handle geometry from an appropriate face.

entries.title: TRAVELER: The Cinematic Hybrid Synthesizer | Official Walkthrough
entries.summary: Official Traveler walkthrough distilled into portable hybrid-synth patch recipes.

skills.name: traveler-walkthrough-control-track-filter-wt-animation
skills.goal: Use dual Control Tracks (sequenced controller lanes) as the heartbeat: up to 16 steps, ping-pong, DAW-synced rates, swing/gate/depth, routing to filter cutoff, wavetable position, or any mod destination.
steps: Open sequencer/Control Tracks panel. Configure Track A: length ≤16 steps, direction forward or ping-pong, tempo-synced note value.
Set Track A destination from the shared mod destination list (same as mod matrix): e.g. filter cutoff or wavetable position. Set depth, gate time, swing.
Configure Track B with a complementary destination and optionally different length/rate for evolving polyrhythmic motion.
Use utilities: copy A→B, reverse/flip, reset, or randomize steps when exploring — then refine by ear.
Optionally pair with arpeggiator: many patterns; can target individual oscillators so one osc arps while another holds a pad; shape arp attacks with mod envelope when per-osc selected.

skills.name: traveler-walkthrough-curved-envelope-evolving-pad
skills.goal: Design a long-evolving cinematic pad using multi-stage envelopes with adjustable curve handles, up to ~20s stages, optional breakpoint/slope expansion, and a modulation envelope that can start from alt control (e.g. sustain pedal) instead of note-on.
steps: Set three envelopes: filter, VCA, and modulation. Open the on-screen envelope editor and drag curve handles on time stages.
Use long time stages (up to ~20s each) for cinematic bloom. Expand envelope to add breakpoint + slope stages (ADBSSR-style) when you need a mid-bloom reshape.
Route filter envelope to stereo LPF cutoff with moderate amount; VCA envelope for amplitude; mod envelope to WT position, pan, or secondary cutoff.
Optional alt-control on mod envelope: start envelope from sustain pedal (or other mod-bus source) instead of key press for expressive delayed motion.
LFOs: choose from varied shapes including unipolar and slew/random; key-sync or free; tempo-sync optional; dedicate pitch or filter vibrato with fade-in on LFO1/2.
Finish with soft EQ, light chorus, long space/hall reverb (space algo up to very long tails). Keep limiter available as safety for dynamic patches.

skills.name: traveler-walkthrough-fx-eq-chorus-delay-reverb
skills.goal: Finish a cinematic patch with the Traveler-style FX order: 3-band EQ → multi-type chorus → dual/ping-pong modulated delay → room/hall/space reverb (long space tails).
steps: Insert 3-band EQ first: sculpt low end, mid presence, and highs so the synth sits in a mix before time FX.
Add chorus: choose type 1, type 2, or combined. Keep wet modest for cinematic width without seasick detune.
Dual or ping-pong stereo modulated delay: independent L/R times, feedback, stereo spread, feedback filters, and classic delay modulation.
Reverb: pick room, hall, or space algorithm (space can reach very long tails). Set size/decay/predelay manually with original settings.
Map portable names: KeyTIME-like = tempo-synced modulated delay motion; KeySPACE-like = multi-algo cinematic reverb. Keep FX after synth engine; watch limiter on main out.

skills.name: traveler-walkthrough-stereo-ladder-lf-width
skills.goal: Shape a cinematic tone with stereo ladder/NJM-style filters, left/right cutoff offset or per-key spread, linked high-pass for band-pass effects, and low-frequency width so bass stays centered while highs move.
steps: Choose ladder-style LPF slope from gentle 6 dB to steep 24 dB (four ladder variants) OR NJM 2069-style model for DW/Poly-era character.
Enable stereo filter path. Offset left vs right cutoff, or use automatic per-key spread, for subtle stereo timbre differences (good automation target).
Add dedicated high-pass; optionally link HP to primary cutoff for band-pass style sweeps. Set keyboard tracking and envelope amounts for both LP and HP.
Output section: set pan-spread so successive voices fan across the stereo field; optional random voice position.
Engage low-frequency width / LF-width: narrow pan of content below ~middle C so bass stays mono-centered while upper spectrum keeps stereo motion.
Optional vintage/voice-offset knob for slight per-voice drift of tune, mixer, filter, envelopes — keep near 0 for clean cinematic pads.

skills.name: traveler-walkthrough-super-unison-wide-lead
skills.goal: Build a gigantic wide lead/pad layer using a multi-voice stereo unison oscillator (Traveler Osc2-style stack up to ~7 voices) with waveform morph and stereo spread.
steps: Assign Oscillator 2 role as the Super/unison stack: continuous waveform from saw through sine to thin pulse.
Enable stereo voice stack (up to ~7 voices). Increase detune and stereo spread until the stack alone sounds gigantic.
Optionally add Osc1 as FM/sync carrier support (sync Osc2; FM from Osc2/3 linear or exponential, variable depth) for bite.
Mixer: set Osc2 level primary; pan can be modulated later. Mild drive into filter if available.
Route through stereo ladder-style LPF (12–24 dB). Keep cutoff high enough to preserve width; use modest resonance.
Amp envelope: medium attack for pads or fast attack for leads; sustain mid-high; release 0.5–2s. Enable pan-spread / voice stereo distribution if available.

skills.name: traveler-walkthrough-wavetable-morph-filter-motion
skills.goal: Create an evolving hybrid patch using a wavetable oscillator (Osc3 role), optional duo-stack/detune/stereo spread, and animated WT position + filter cutoff.
steps: Osc3 role: switch from analog waveforms to wavetable mode. Load an original/freely available WT (do not import Traveler proprietary tables).
Optional: enable 2-voice stack, detune, and stereo spread on the WT osc for width.
Optional drone mode: disconnect Osc3 from keyboard for a fixed-pitch layer, or use it as an extra LFO-rate modulator.
Modulate wavetable position from LFO or Control Track; keep depth subtle for evolving texture rather than obvious sweeps unless desired.
Stereo filter: ladder model (6–24 dB) or NJM-style; add HP that can link to primary cutoff for band-pass motion. Modulate cutoff from filter envelope and/or LFO.
Mixer: balance WT vs analog oscs; add noise (white/pink) sparingly; light drive into filter.

entries.title: TRAVELER Track Walkthrough by Venus Theory
entries.summary: Venus Theory production techniques for evolving cinematic sequences and hybrid impacts.

skills.name: keysol-venus-fifths-pulsar-wt-impact
skills.goal: Craft a throbbing aggressive impact/pulse by tuning a second oscillator up a fifth (+7 semitones), adding duo/detune/scatter width, and a wavetable layer for dimension beyond plain VA.
steps: Build throbbing aggressive core on Osc1 (pulse/saw). Set Osc2 +7 semitones for fifths power; balance for deep power vs mid punch vs brighter transient emphasis.
Enable duo/unison, detune, and stereo scatter/spread for width.
Add wavetable oscillator not as a full replacement but as dimensional spice; animate WT position for movement.
Play velocity-reactive syncopated rhythms into a bouncing delay so the part stays alive across long phrases.

skills.name: keysol-venus-fm-lfo-evolving-chase-sequence
skills.goal: Keep long cinematic chase/arp-like sequences alive by modulating FM depth, oscillator mix via LFOs, and filter cutoff — plus mod-wheel/aftertouch for tension — instead of static one-bar loops.
steps: Establish rhythmic pulse/sequence foundation (arp or control-track → cutoff). Aim for cinematic intensity rather than clean EDM purity.
Introduce FM: vary modulator frequency slightly and automate/modulate FM depth so timbre breathes over the phrase.
Use LFOs to change oscillator mix balances over time; also modulate filter cutoff so the sequence refuses to feel static across long cues.
Assign mod wheel / aftertouch to open tension (depth, cutoff, or drive) for scene dynamics.
Play deeper registers for more body when the cue needs weight; keep FX (delay bounce) feeding syncopated rhythms for living grooves.

skills.name: keysol-venus-high-wt-artifact-pulse-layer
skills.goal: Spice a classic pulsing bass/filter sequence by adding a very high-pitched wavetable oscillator mixed as an artifact-like layer, with WT-position modulation for constant subtle evolution.
steps: Build a classic pulsating bass sequence: pulse/saw bed, Control Track or LFO → filter cutoff, use filter feedback/saturation/drive for grit and presence.
Add wavetable oscillator tuned very high until it reads almost as an artifact rather than a clear tone.
Modulate wavetable position slowly (LFO or Control Track) for continuous micro-variation so the sequence never feels static.
Mix WT low under the pulse bed; A/B with WT muted to confirm it adds interest without dominating.

skills.name: keysol-venus-noise-audiorate-filter-texture
skills.goal: Create a radioactive/unstable cinematic texture or lead: dual detuned saws + WT character, aftertouch bringing in a sharp high oscillator, and mod-wheel sending noise (~30% mix) into audio-rate-style filter modulation (plus optional Osc2→cutoff always-on grit).
steps: Layer two fairly separate saw oscillators plus a wavetable osc for character. Slightly detune one osc; further detune can yield ring-mod-like artifacts.
Optionally enable continuous Osc2 → low-pass cutoff (audio-rate-ish FM-of-filter) for granular grit; A/B it to hear the instability.
Mix noise around ~30%. Map mod wheel to send noise into LPF cutoff modulation — annihilating cutoff with noise yields extremely unstable/distorted color.
Use aftertouch (or pressure) to bring in a high-frequency oscillator for resonant overtones that feel like distortion byproducts when played low.
Play as lead, texture, or pre-scare sting; leave headroom — this patch is intentionally unstable.

skills.name: keysol-venus-polyrhythmic-control-track-pitch
skills.goal: Build a never-quite-repeating cinematic sequence by driving Osc1/Osc2 pitch from two Control Tracks with irregular lengths (e.g. 15 and 14) and independent rates (e.g. dotted quarter vs quarter), over a stable low Osc3 pulse bed.
steps: Create a stable bed on Osc3 (e.g. pulse) an octave or two below; add delay/space lightly so the bed feels cinematic but steady.
Raise Osc1 and Osc2 to much higher pitch registers; they need not sound pretty alone — they supply character over the bed.

Control Track A → Osc1 pitch, length 15, rate dotted-quarter (or similar). Control Track B → Osc2 pitch, length 14, rate quarter. Keep modulation depth small so pitch breaks subtly rather than jumping wildly.
Map mod wheel (or expression) to increase the depth of those pitch mods for performance tension.
Mix: keep Osc3 dominant; blend high oscs underneath. Solo high pair to verify the irregular interlocking, then restore full mix.

skills.name: keysol-venus-velocity-hybrid-bass-impact
skills.goal: Design a thunderous hybrid bass/impact that responds exponentially to velocity (louder hits open filter/amp dramatically), usable as deep hits or high atmospheric stabs with HP + long space reverb.
steps: Start with dark hybrid oscillators (saw/pulse + optional WT). Fast amp attack, punchy decay, moderate sustain for bass; shorter for impacts.
Map velocity strongly (near-exponential) to filter cutoff and/or drive so louder playing blooms dramatically.
For atmospheric use: apply aggressive high-pass on the mix, play high register with pitch bend, and use a broad smooth space-style reverb so hits become huge pads/stingers.
For deep bass: keep HP low/off, emphasize transient, optionally underscoring with sub; avoid static sine-only subs — keep some transient character.

steps: Create a simple two-layer patch: mid/high tonal oscillator(s) plus a dedicated low oscillator.
Modulate the low oscillator’s volume with keyboard tracking so it is strong only in the lower register (left hand / low keys) and fades as you play higher.
Set delay wet very high (delay almost louder than the dry sound) to showcase modulation/space; filter delay feedback to taste.

entries.title: How to Sharpen a Chisel | Paul Sellers
entries.summary: How to initialize a new chisel: factory edges are only ground to about 150-200 grit. Flatten and polish just the back near the edge through coarse, medium and superfine (1200) stones, polish it on a compound-charged wood strop, then sharpen the bevel at the factory angle through the grits until an even burr forms, remove the burr, and strop on charged leather. Later sharpening repeats only the bevel steps.

entries.title: How to get PERFECT First Layers on Your 3D Printer!!
entries.summary: First-layer adhesion depends on Z offset as much as bed leveling. Square the gantry and level the bed first, then set the offset so lines touch and look glass-smooth (too far: lines don't touch; too close: ridges). Adjust on the printer while printing and keep the slicer global offset at 0; lower a too-high Z limit switch (then retighten springs and relevel); clean the bed with alcohol; prioritize the center on a warped bed or replace it and consider an auto-leveling probe with hard-mounted bed.

entries.title: How to Patch a Drywall Hole | Ask This Old House
